authority_limit: JSON Schema and SHACL structural constraints do not establish complete domain semantics or business authority.
bounded_claim: Constraint/assertion definitions state conditions an instance/data graph must satisfy, while validation execution produces a separate boolean/report/result artifact.
negative_twin: A constraint can exist without ever being executed, and a successful validation report only proves the constraints that were actually declared and evaluated.

authority_limit: OCL constrains UML/model instances and operations; it does not prove runtime enforcement or business authorization.
bounded_claim: OCL distinguishes invariant constraints from operation preconditions and postconditions, giving them different semantic scopes and evaluation times.
negative_twin: An operation can be authorized yet invalid because its semantic precondition is false, or execute while later violating a postcondition.

authority_limit: Database constraints enforce declared storage predicates, not all application/domain invariants.
bounded_claim: Relational systems distinguish CHECK, UNIQUE, PRIMARY KEY, FOREIGN KEY and EXCLUSION constraints, including relation-spanning referential integrity and different enforcement semantics.
negative_twin: A database can satisfy every declared foreign key and check constraint while violating a business invariant that was never encoded.

authority_limit: These systems have different enforcement models and do not establish one universal enforcement mechanism.
bounded_claim: Constraint definition and constraint enforcement/validation are distinct. PostgreSQL permits deferrable and selected NOT ENFORCED constraints; SHACL separately defines shapes and validation processing/results.
negative_twin: A documented NOT ENFORCED constraint can define intended validity while current stored data violates it.

authority_limit: Representation/schema validity still does not imply domain truth or acceptance.
bounded_claim: Well-formed representation and validity against declared constraints are distinct notions; a syntactically well-formed document may fail validity constraints.
negative_twin: A well-formed XML or JSON document can be invalid against its schema or semantically wrong despite schema validity.

authority_limit: Schema dialect selection does not establish domain-owner ratification or compatibility with another constraint system.
bounded_claim: Constraint semantics are scoped by declared schema vocabulary/dialect/profile and extensions; the same serialized keyword/token cannot be interpreted outside its declared constraint language context.
negative_twin: A custom or optional vocabulary keyword can be ignored or interpreted differently by processors that do not support the same dialect/profile.
